question: How many dry-weather tyres can a Hypercar use for qualifying and the race at a 6-hour race?
expected_answer: 18 dry-weather tyres for qualifying + race at a 6-hour race (plus 4 for Hyperpole and 12 for free practice).

question: How many tyres can an LMGT3 car use in free practice?
expected_answer: 16 dry-weather tyres in free practice. Wet-weather tyres are not limited.

question: How many different dry tyre specifications can Hypercar teams use over the season?
expected_answer: 3 dry-weather specifications over the season (3 at the 24H Le Mans, 2 at other races) and 1 wet-weather specification.

question: What is the fine for driving at 63 km/h in the pit lane during practice?
expected_answer: A fine of €500 (speed between 60 and 65 km/h during practice and warm-up; the limit is 60 km/h).

question: What is the penalty for a first offence of 75 km/h in the pit lane during the race?
expected_answer: A Stop & Go of 5 seconds per km/h above 70 km/h, i.e. 25 seconds (for the 1st and 2nd infringement at 70 km/h or more).

question: How many points does the winner of a 6-hour race score?
expected_answer: 25 points.

question: How many points do you get for finishing 10th at the 24 Hours of Le Mans?
expected_answer: 2 points.

question: What is the minimum driving time for a Bronze driver in an 8-hour LMGT3 race?
expected_answer: 2h20 (same for Silver drivers; 1h45 for a 6h race and 2h55 for a 10h race).

question: Which championship titles are awarded in the LMGT3 category?
expected_answer: The FIA Endurance Trophy for LMGT3 Drivers and the FIA Endurance Trophy for LMGT3 Teams.

question: What environmental accreditation level do Hypercar teams need in 2026?
expected_answer: 3 stars in the FIA Environmental Accreditation Programme (2 stars for LMGT3).

question: What is the penalty if the cockpit temperature goes over the limit during the race?
expected_answer: Stop & repair (black and orange flag), every time it happens.

question: What happens the second time a Hypercar's pit launch release time is below the BoP limit?
expected_answer: 10 seconds are added to its next pit stop (5 s the 1st time, 20 s from the 3rd time).

question: How many operational staff can a two-car LMDh team have?
expected_answer: 50 people.

question: How many dry tyres can a manufacturer use per year for its own manufacturer tests?
expected_answer: The table gives '120 (30)' for manufacturer tests (by manufacturer), under the heading 'Yearly allocation (Sets)'; the document does not state the unit of each number. Transport tyres are not counted.

question: Can teams use tools while the car is being refuelled?
expected_answer: No. Tools are not allowed during the refuelling phase.

question: How many mechanics can work on the car during a pit stop?
expected_answer: A maximum of four persons wearing the appropriate armband, plus up to two industry representatives/technicians who may only check tyres and brakes.

question: Does the engine have to be switched off for a driver change?
expected_answer: Yes. The car must be properly stopped, engine off, in its dedicated stopping area.

question: How quickly must a team send its car data to the Technical Delegates after entering the pit lane?
expected_answer: At the latest 10 minutes after the car entered the pit lane (or 30 minutes after the end of the race).

question: Can a team change a fuel flow meter during a race weekend?
expected_answer: Not without prior approval from the Technical Delegate; a removed sensor may be kept by the Technical Delegate.

question: How many team members can go onto the grid when a red-flagged race is about to restart?
expected_answer: A maximum of 4 personnel per car, wearing the appropriate armbands, from the '15 minutes' signal, for a limited list of tasks.

question: How long is Hyperpole and which cars take part?
expected_answer: At least 10 minutes; it is reserved for the 10 best cars of the first qualifying session of the category and sets the first 10 grid positions.

question: What penalty does a car get for starting the race from the pit lane?
expected_answer: 1 minute added to its next pit stop.

question: How big is the stopping area in front of the garage?
expected_answer: Drawing N°1: the stopping area is 250 cm deep inside a 500 cm wide working area, 50 cm from the 2.5 m line.

question: What is the minimum size of the Michelin logos on the sides of a Hypercar?
expected_answer: 1 Michelin logo on each side, at least 35 cm wide (or 1 Michelin Man decal per side, at least 20 cm high); at least one Michelin logo per side is mandatory.

question: Where must the RFID tyre stickers be placed on the car?
expected_answer: On each side, in front of the rear wheel at about wheel-axis height; if not possible, behind the rear wheel; otherwise where the Technical Delegate decides.

question: What driver licence do you need to race in the Hypercar category?
expected_answer: FIA Grade A (minimum Grade B for the other categories).

question: Who counts as a manufacturer under the Hypercar testing rules?
expected_answer: The one who homologates a car.

question: Does cranking the engine count as starting it?
expected_answer: Yes, any cranking operation is considered as starting the engine.

question: From which signal must the green armband be worn on the grid during a race suspension?
expected_answer: The text says 'from the 10 15 minute signal': the published document is ambiguous (10 or 15 minutes). The answer must say so rather than choose.

question: What happens if a car enters its garage during its own qualifying session?
expected_answer: A penalty of cancellation of the lap times set before entering the garage; the text says 'will may be imposed', so whether it is automatic is ambiguous and the answer must say so.

question: Which language version of the regulations applies in case of a dispute?
expected_answer: The French version.

question: Do these regulations apply to the 24 Hours of Le Mans?
expected_answer: Le Mans is governed by its own Supplementary Regulations, which take precedence over these regulations in all aspects.

question: What happens if a driver exceeds the track limits?
expected_answer: A penalty at the Stewards' discretion, which may go as far as disqualification of the driver, in practice and in the race.

question: What is the speed limit under a Full Course Yellow?
expected_answer: 80 km/h, in single file, without overtaking.

question: How fast must cars go under the Virtual Safety Car?
expected_answer: 80 km/h, in a single line, no overtaking; a VSC period is always followed by a Safety Car procedure.

question: What is the penalty for doing a Pass-Around when the car is not eligible?
expected_answer: A Stop & Go for a time equal to two race laps.

question: Do you get a point for pole position?
expected_answer: Yes, 1 extra point for the team and all its drivers, for the best Hyperpole time in each category.

question: What percentage of the race distance must a car cover to be classified?
expected_answer: At least 70% of the distance covered by the overall winner, and it must cross the line when the chequered flag is shown.

question: How much does it cost to lodge a protest?
expected_answer: A deposit of €1,000.

question: Can the driver get out of the car during a Stop & Go penalty?
expected_answer: No. The driver must remain on board and no operation is allowed on the car.

question: How long before a race are teams banned from testing on that circuit?
expected_answer: 30 days before the start of the Competition.

question: Is the Prologue test mandatory?
expected_answer: Yes, for all cars of competitors entered for the full season.

question: How much does the on-board camera system weigh?
expected_answer: 3.8 kg; cars without a camera must carry ballast.

question: Can a Bronze driver race in the Hypercar category?
expected_answer: No. Hypercar crews are free provided they include no Bronze driver.

question: What are the driver line-up rules for an LMGT3 crew?
expected_answer: A crew of two or three drivers must include at least one Bronze driver plus another Bronze or a Silver driver.

question: Can mechanics help restart a car that stops on track during the race?
expected_answer: No. The engine must be restarted by the driver alone, with the starter or other on-board equipment.

question: What are mechanics allowed to do in parc fermé after the race?
expected_answer: One mechanic may connect/disconnect a power supply for cooling or place external cooling devices, and safety work on hybrid systems is allowed; nothing else.

question: How big a gap between the TPMS reading and the manual gauge gets reported to the stewards?
expected_answer: When the TPMS signal is higher than the manual gauge reading by more than 0.03 bar.

question: When and where is the 2026 Rookie Test?
expected_answer: 8 November 2026 in Bahrain.

question: How much must a Hypercar team pay in advance for fuel and technical costs?
expected_answer: €60,000 on 13 February 2026 and €60,000 on 22 May 2026; unused amounts are returned after the last Competition.
